page: Amazon Web Services c8i.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. It features 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores with hyper-threading) running at 3.9 GHz, backed by a 480 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core performance, with Geekbench multi-core and software compilation tests placing in the top 10% tier. The processor's support for advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), accelerates vector and matrix operations. This is reflected in strong LLM inference speeds, particularly for prompt processing on medium-sized 7B models, which ranks in the top 10% tier. Static web serving throughput also achieves top-tier status, while large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 197.26 GB/sec.

Given its compute-heavy configuration and high-speed DDR5 memory, the c8i.16xlarge offers high resource density for CPU-bound tasks without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPUs. It is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, image processing, high-throughput web serving, and medium-scale machine learning inference. However, memory-bound applications requiring more than 2 GB of RAM per core or workloads dependent on local NVMe storage may face performance tradeoffs.
